item.title: [7] Nature of the bosonic edge phase in a double quantum spin Hall insulator
item.description:
Last authors: Nicolas Regnault, Julian May-Mann

Authors: Andreas Feuerpfeil, Ronny Thomale, Trithep Devakul, Nicolas Regnault, Julian May-Mann

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Relevant study of interaction-driven topological edge phases in WSe2 and MoTe2 twisted bilayers.

Tags: #theory #twisted-bilayers #WSe2 #topology

Abstract: Field-theoretic analysis has predicted that the edge of a double quantum spin Hall insulator (DQSHI) can undergo an interaction-driven transition from a phase with fermionic edge modes into one with only bosonic modes. All single-fermion edge excitations are gapped in this bosonic edge phase, but fermion pairs remain gapless, leading to distinct experimental signatures. We numerically simulate the interacting DQSHI edge and verify the existence of the bosonic edge phase. This calculation requires an explicit bulk embedding of the DQSHI edge, due to its mixed anomaly between charge and $S^z$ conservation. We hence employ segment DMRG on an infinite two-dimensional cylinder, where the DQSHI bulk is modeled in terms of two copies of the spin-up lowest Landau level, combined with their time-reversed counterparts. We find that interactions can open a single-fermion gap at the DQSHI edge while fermion pairs remain gapless, matching the predictions for the bosonic edge phase. We find the scaling of the single-fermion gap with interaction strength to be consistent with field-theoretic calculations, and discuss the relevance of the bosonic edge phase to twisted homobilayers of WSe$_2$ and MoTe$_2$. We elaborate on the methodological extension of the segment geometry used here to other topological phases with edge anomalies.

item.title: [9] Charge-monitored Luttinger liquid
item.description:
Last authors: Victor Gurarie, Leo Radzihovsky

Score 9/10 A_MUST_READ

Why: title strong match: Luttinger liquid

Tags: #Luttinger #superconduct

Abstract: We discuss phases of interacting fermionic Luttinger liquids without particle number conservation, such as those in proximity to a superconductor, subjected to weak continuous measurements of their particle density, in the regime where the bosonization approach is applicable. We show that the phases of these systems are controlled by the competition between measurements, which favor the area-law phase and particle tunneling in and out of the Luttinger liquid, which favors the volume-law phase. The volume-law phase in this system is always charge fuzzy. We show that within this framework, the phase boundary between the two phases is given by a universal dependence of the Luttinger parameter on the measurement rate. This behavior can be contrasted with the non-universal phase boundaries in more generic highly excited one dimensional systems whose behavior is no longer captured by the Luttinger liquid framework.

item.title: [8] Charge Density Waves and In-Gap States in Coupled Chains and Moir\'e Superlattices
item.description:
Last authors: Muhammad Akram, Onur Erten

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Highly relevant theoretical study of CDW and bound states in 1D and moiré systems.

Tags: #theory #CDW #1D-chains #moiré

Abstract: Charge density waves (CDWs) arise from the interplay between electrons and lattice distortions and are a hallmark of low-dimensional systems. Here we study coupled Su-Schrieffer-Heeger chains, both lattice-matched ladders and lattice-mismatched moir\'e superlattices, and find a rich set of CDW phases together with symmetry-protected bound states. In lattice-matched chains, the competition between electron-phonon coupling and interchain tunneling drives a sequence of CDW phases, including staggered dimers, trimers, and incommensurate states. These phases are generally gapped and host bound states protected by crystalline symmetries rather than chiral symmetry, and are therefore not pinned to zero energy. Lattice mismatch further reconstructs these phases into long-period supermoir\'e CDWs, with an ordered array of defects, pinned to the moir\'e length scale, that host localized electronic states. Interchain tunneling and lattice mismatch thus emerge as natural control parameters for CDW order and bound states in one-dimensional chains.

item.title: [7] Extreme competition between stripes and superconductivity in the hole-doped Hubbard model
item.description:
Last authors: Si-Jing Du, Garnet Kin-Lic Chan

Authors: Ao Chen, Johnnie Gray, Si-Jing Du, Garnet Kin-Lic Chan

Score 7/10 C_MAYBE

Why: Addresses high-accuracy competition between d-wave superconductivity and stripes in cuprate-relevant models.; tier capped to C: formal/generic theory watch

Tags: #theory #cuprate #superconductivity #Hubbard-model

Abstract: The two-dimensional Hubbard model was originally proposed as the minimal model of uniform $d$-wave superconductivity in the cuprate high-temperature superconductors, but recent calculations with relevant parameters in a realistic doping regime have often found other ground states. Further, uncertainty remains over such results due to the intrinsic bias of different computational methods. Here we address this uncertainty through state-of-the-art neural tensor network and neural backflow state simulations, enabled by large-scale GPU computation, that together reach an unprecedented variational accuracy on lattices with up to 1024 sites. At $1/8$ doping in the pure Hubbard model, as well as with next-nearest-neighbor hopping relevant to the hole-doped cuprates, we reveal a near degeneracy among a low-energy uniform $d$-wave state, superconducting stripes, and non-superconducting stripe states on the milli-$t$ energy scale. Our work rebalances the narrative that the Hubbard model supports a single dominant order in relevant parameter regimes towards a picture of extreme competition between stripes and superconductivity.

item.title: [9] Emergent altermagnetism in (LaVO3)n/(LaNiO3)m superlattices from interfacial charge transfer and octahedral tilts
item.description:
Last authors: Gustavo H. Cassemiro, Walber H. Brito

Score 9/10 A_MUST_READ

Why: Direct hit on altermagnetism and nickelate heterostructures; high relevance for electronic structure and transport.

Tags: #theory #altermagnetism #nickelate #heterostructure

Abstract: Using first-principles calculations, we show that altermagnetism emerges in (LaVO$_3$)$_n$/(LaNiO$_3$)$_m$ superlattices, with $(n,m) = (1,1), (2,2)$ and $(2,4)$, from the interplay of interfacial charge transfer and octahedral tilts. Charge transfer drives the system towards the V$^{4+}$ and Ni$^{2+}$ configuration, turning the otherwise paramagnetic nickelate layers into a magnetically active sublattice. The resulting $C$-type antiferromagnetic order, combined with $a^-b^+c^-$ or $a^-b^-c^-$ octahedral tilts, links opposite-spin sublattices only through nonsymmorphic operations, yielding a $d$-wave spin splitting without spin-orbit coupling. Within DFT+U, the splitting reaches 118 meV in the insulating (LVO)$_1$/(LNO)$_1$ superlattice, about twice that calculated for bulk LaVO$_3$, and decreases as the nickelate layers become thicker. Our findings indicate that this splitting is hosted by both the V and Ni sublattices, with nearly half of its weight on oxygen $2p$ states through $p$-$d$ covalency. Interfacial charge transfer thus emerges as a \textit{design} principle for engineering altermagnetism in oxide heterostructures.

item.title: [7] Anisotropic thermoelectric transport in the Sr2RuO4-Ru eutectic system
item.description:
Last authors: Hiroshi Yaguchi, Ryuji Okazaki

Authors: Takeru Ito, Shogo Yoshida, Hiroshi Yaguchi, Ryuji Okazaki

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Investigates strain-induced electronic structure changes and Fermi surface modifications in Sr2RuO4.

Tags: #superconductivity #Sr2RuO4 #electronic-structure

Abstract: The Sr2RuO4-Ru eutectic system, in which metallic Ru inclusions are embedded in a Sr2RuO4 matrix, exhibits an enhanced superconducting onset temperature of about 3 K, known as the 3-K phase. Here we investigate the in-plane thermoelectric response of this eutectic system in the normal state and find a pronounced anisotropy in the thermopower for thermal gradients applied parallel and perpendicular to the Ru lamellae. To clarify its origin, we combine thermopower measurements with electronic-structure-based transport calculations and finite-element modeling of the local strain distribution generated by the thermal-expansion mismatch between Sr2RuO4 and Ru. The calculations show that uniaxial compression of Sr2RuO4 produces a sizable thermopower anisotropy through modification of the Fermi surfaces. When an idealized spatially inhomogeneous strain field around the Ru lamellae is included, the observed sign and qualitative magnitude of the anisotropy are reproduced more closely than in a simple unstrained two-component model. These results are consistent with a substantial contribution from strain-induced changes in the Sr2RuO4 electronic structure near the interfaces, although contributions from interfacial phase mixing and three-dimensional transport connectivity cannot be excluded.

item.title: [7] Field-free superconducting diode and tunable vortex dynamics in NbN/FePt stripe-domain heterostructures
item.description:
Last authors: Jeehoon Kim, Nestor Haberkorn

Authors: Juan C. Zapata, Emilio De Biasi, Martin Sirena, Jeehoon Kim, Nestor Haberkorn

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Experimental study of superconducting nonreciprocity and vortex dynamics in magnetic heterostructures.

Tags: #superconductivity #heterostructure #transport

Abstract: We demonstrate reconfigurable, field-free superconducting diode behavior in NbN/FePt and NbN/AlN/FePt heterostructures with remanent stripe domains in the FePt layer. NbN films 10 nm thick are capped either directly with FePt or through a thin AlN spacer, which reduces electronic proximity effects while preserving magnetic coupling through stray fields. At zero applied magnetic field, the superconducting diode efficiency reaches approximately 50--60% in NbN/FePt when the stripes are perpendicular to the current and is strongly reduced when they are parallel. The diode effect persists in NbN/AlN/FePt with efficiencies reaching approximately 35--40%, supporting a magnetic origin of the nonreciprocity. We interpret the response as asymmetric vortex transport in the remanent magnetic landscape, with preferential edge vorticity and a Lorentz force that favors inward flux injection or outward motion depending on current polarity. Under applied perpendicular magnetic fields, the interplay between the external field and the magnetic stray fields modifies the flux-flow instability and the apparent instability velocity inferred from transport, with values below those reported for bare NbN films. These results show that stripe-domain ferromagnetic overlayers provide a reconfigurable route to control superconducting nonreciprocity and flux-flow stability in NbN-based heterostructures.

item.title: [9] Impact of localized 4f magnetism on Berry curvature and the intrinsic anomalous Hall effect in CeRu2Si2
item.description:
Last authors: Ibuki Terada, Michi-To Suzuki

Authors: Takehiro Kobayashi, Shunsuke Hirai, Ibuki Terada, Michi-To Suzuki

Score 9/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Direct study of Berry curvature and anomalous Hall in a specific f-electron electronic structure.

Tags: #electronic-structure #Berry-curvature #anomalous-Hall

Abstract: The intrinsic anomalous Hall effect (AHE), originating from Berry curvature, has been extensively studied in $f$-electron systems, including Ce-based compounds. However, how the magnetism of localized $f$ electrons affect the intrinsic AHE remains unclear. Here, we investigate this issue in CeRu$_2$Si$_2$ by calculating the intrinsic anomalous Hall conductivity (AHC) for several occupied Ce-$4f$ states using first-principles LDA+$U$ calculations combined with Wannier interpolation method. We find that the intrinsic AHC remains finite even when the Ce-$4f$ states are localized and do not contribute directly to the Fermi surface, and that its magnitude depends on which Ce-$4f$ state is occupied. We show that localized $4f$-electron magnetism induces exchange splitting in the conduction bands, generating Berry curvature in specific regions near the Fermi surface. This mechanism enables conduction bands that are derived from nonmagnetic orbitals and form the Fermi surface to contribute to the intrinsic AHE, suggesting a route to realizing large intrinsic AHE in $f$-electron materials.

item.title: [8] Ferroelastic Reversal Magnon Thermal Hall Effect in a Fully Compensated Ferrimagnet
item.description:
Last authors: Chengwang Niu, Ming Yang

Authors: Yingxi Bai, Zihan Chen, Chengwang Niu, Ming Yang

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Connects altermagnetism, Berry curvature, and transport in a monolayer system.

Tags: #altermagnetism #Berry-curvature #monolayer

Abstract: Magnons offer a charge-neutral channel for spin and heat transport, yet reversible and nonvolatile control of their thermal Hall response poses a fundamental challenge in systems with zero net magnetization. Here, we establish ferroelastic switching as an effective route to manipulate magnonic transverse responses in fully compensated ferrimagnets. A minimal Heisenberg-Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya model reveals that ferroelastic switching can re-orientate the lattice anisotropy, which reconstructs the chirality-resolved magnon bands and Berry curvature distribution. Consequently, the two orthogonal fully compensated ferrimagnetic variants related by [C2||C4z] exhibit magnon thermal Hall responses with opposite signs, whereas the response vanishes in the intermediate altermagnetic phase. First-principles calculations further identify monolayer V2SSe as a promising material candidate for realizing the proposed ferroelastic control of transverse magnon transport. Remarkably, ferroelastic switching drives a dual magnonic-electronic band reconstruction, enabling nonvolatile reversal of the magnon thermal Hall effect while producing anisotropic orbital Hall responses and distinct magneto-optical spectra as complementary transport and optical fingerprints. Our findings establish ferroelasticity as an effective route to nonvolatile magnon control and multichannel state identification in zero net magnetization systems.

item.title: [7] Anyon Chern bands of opposite sign and reversed drift
item.description:
Last authors: Minxuan Wang, Shinsei Ryu

Authors: Zhenyu Xiao, Minxuan Wang, Shinsei Ryu

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Broadly relevant theory of topological anyon motion and Berry curvature in Chern insulators.

Tags: #topology #Chern-insulator #anyons

Abstract: The elementary charged excitations of fractional quantum Hall states are anyons. Without continuous translation symmetry, they acquire a dispersion and richer dynamics. We study the Laughlin quasihole at filling $1/3$ in a periodically modulated magnetic field, a common model of fractional Chern insulators in two-dimensional materials. From the microscopic wave functions, we derive the commutator of its guiding-center coordinates, set by a many-body Berry curvature that governs its wave packets. A modulation with two flux quanta per unit cell splits the quasihole band into bands with Chern numbers $6$ and $-3$; such opposite signs are generic as long as a weak modulation opens a gap between the anyon bands. In the $C=-3$ band, the quasihole drifts against $\mathbf{E}\times\mathbf{B}$, although the magnetic field has the same sign everywhere. Perturbation theory in the modulation explains these results, and large-scale Monte Carlo calculations confirm them. Anyon bands thus acquire their own topology, which controls anyon motion and may shape the phases of itinerant anyons.

item.title: [9] Coulomb-Driven Electronic Textures in Lightly Hole-Doped Cuprates
item.description:
Last authors: Mingpu Qin, Kun Jiang

Authors: Wei-Wei Yang, Yang Shen, Yuxin Wang, Pengfei Li, Mingpu Qin, Kun Jiang

Score 9/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Theory of electronic textures in cuprates with strong relevance to STM/STS observations.

Tags: #cuprates #electronic-structure #STM

Abstract: Motivated by recent experiments on Ca$_2$CuO$_2$Cl$_2$, we present a comprehensive study of the interplay between dopants and localized Zhang-Rice singlets in lightly hole-doped cuprates. Owing to the poorly screened Coulomb potential, the interactions between dopants and localized Zhang-Rice singlets favor asymmetric electronic configurations characterized by effective electric "dipoles". Using the MPS-based Lanczos method, we show that these localized holes give rise to in-gap bound states within the charge-transfer gap. When tunneling matrix-element effects are included, the bound states exhibit a characteristic $4a_0 \times 2a_0$ internal structure, consistent with experimental observations. Our results suggest that Coulomb interactions between dopants and localized Zhang-Rice singlets, together with tunneling matrix-element effects, provide a microscopic mechanism for the observed $4a_0$ electronic structures.

item.description:
Last authors: Fabio Caruso, Samuel Beaulieu

Abstract: The type-II Dirac semimetals PtSe$_2$ and PtTe$_2$ are isostructural and isovalent layered compounds but exhibit distinct electronic properties. In PtTe$_2$, the chalcogen-$p$ band lies higher in energy, which lowers the onset of these transitions and increases the semimetallic band overlap, in line with the larger Drude spectral weight. item.title: [7] Occupancy Driven Phase Transitions in Gapped Systems
item.description:
Last authors: Alex Kociubinski, Wouter Montfrooij

Authors: Ian Madden, Alex Kociubinski, Wouter Montfrooij

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Theoretical framework for phase transitions applied to the hidden order in URu2Si2.

Tags: #material #topic

Abstract: Systems characterized by an energy gap between the ground state and excited states support a growing number of thermal excitations upon raising the temperature. Provided these excitations interact with each other, their number affects the size of the energy gap akin to a harmonic oscillator where the oscillation frequency is damping dependent. Here we show that once a critical number of excitations is reached, the excitation population becomes thermodynamically unstable and the system transitions between two states. This transition is marked by a divergence in the specific heat, which does not have to be accompanied by an order parameter, nor by the full closure of the gap. We illustrate the thermodynamics using a simple two level system and superfluid $^4$He as examples, and we argue that the hidden order transition in URu$_2$Si$_2$ is an example of such an occupancy driven transition in the absence of an order parameter.

item.description:
Last authors: Xiao Liu, Ed Saunders

Abstract: The charge neutrality point (CNP) of graphene nanoribbons (GNRs) patterned by oxygen plasma etching moves towards zero as the ribbon narrows and, on 300 nm SiO2, changes sign below a crossover width of ~ 50 nm: an observation previously attributed to n-type edges surrounding a p-type bulk. We test this edge-doping hypothesis in three ways. First, finite element modelling of complete GNR transistors with uniform doping shows that fringing of the gate field at the edges reproduces the trend of the measured CNP with width down to ~ 50nm without any edge doping, while producing a bias-dependent inversion of the carrier type at the edges that mimics n-type edges in scanned-probe measurements. Second, fitting the CNP of ribbons on 90 nm and 300 nm SiO2 with the gate capacitance of a finite strip, which fixes the electrostatic contribution with no adjustable parameter other than the bulk doping, shows that fringing accounts for most of the width dependence and isolates the remainder as an edge charge. This is acceptor-like (0.24 e/nm per edge) in the present ribbons, which therefore have no n-type edges, and donor-like but small in devices on 300 nm SiO2; no single edge-charge, field-coupled or contact-doping mechanism describes both. Third, scanning gate microscopy finds no edge contrast of the sign expected for n-type edges. The width dependence of the CNP is therefore predominantly electrostatic, and n-type edges are not an intrinsic consequence of oxygen-plasma etching. A design map shows that fringing dominates the width dependence whenever the gate dielectric is thicker than 30-50 nm, whereas in scaled high-K transistors, edge charge dominates and would shift the threshold voltage of a 10 nm ribbon by ~ 0.1-0.15 V. Fitting the CNP versus width with the strip capacitance provides a simple test for edge doping in any gated two-dimensional nanostructure

Abstract: Moir\'e superlattices of transition-metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) host strongly interacting Bose-Fermi mixtures in which bosonic excitons coexist with correlated electron lattices. Using ultrafast, time- and energy-resolved photoluminescence (PL) microscopy, we show that strong exciton-electron and exciton-exciton repulsion can enable ballistic exciton transport in a WSe$_2$/WS$_2$ heterobilayer. It further confirms that strong cross-species interactions allow the electron crystal to perforate the exciton Mott background, enhancing exciton motion. item.description:
Last authors: Clemens Ulrich, Rajendra S. Dhaka

Authors: Ajay Kumar, Clemens Ulrich, Rajendra S. Dhaka

Why: Experimental study of lattice dynamics and correlations in an antiferromagnetic double perovskite.

Interestingly, pronounced changes in the phonon frequencies, linewidths, and intensities are observed around 60~K, well above the long-range antiferromagnetic ordering temperature, $T_{\rm N} \approx 15$~K. These anomalies indicate a modification of the lattice dynamics that may involve local structural distortions, short-range magnetic correlations, or an interplay between them. Moreover, the EXAFS analysis reveals correlated changes in bond distances and Debye--Waller factors around the Co ions near 60~K and 160~K, indicating subtle local structural distortions at temperatures corresponding to the Raman anomalies. The combined Raman and EXAFS results therefore demonstrate a close correlation between anomalous lattice dynamics and local structural evolution in SrLaCoNbO$_6$.

item.title: [9] Dynamical Nonrelativistic Spin Splitting via THz Nonlinear Phononics
item.description:
Last authors: Ankit Disa, James M. Rondinelli

Authors: Linding Yuan, ChanJu You, Ankit Disa, James M. Rondinelli

Score 9/10 A_MUST_READ

Why: DFT and nonlinear phononics study for ultrafast control of nonrelativistic spin splitting in altermagnets.

Tags: #theory #altermagnetism #antiferromagnetism #phonons #DFT #Floquetengineering

Abstract: Nonrelativistic spin splitting (NRSS) in collinear antiferromagnets, including altermagnets and compensated ferrimagnets, offers a route to high-frequency spintronics immune to stray fields, but its dynamic control has remained elusive. We demonstrate, using density functional theory (DFT) and nonlinear phononics, that THz laser pulses can achieve ultrafast, reversible control of NRSS on picosecond timescales in antiferromagnets. We derive two mode-selection criteria, accounting for phonon and magnetic wavevector compatibility and inversion parity, to identify which phonon modes can activate NRSS. While practical implementation depends on excitation conditions, lattice dynamics, and mode coupling, these results establish design principles for identifying materials with stronger and more accessible responses. item.title: [7] Parity-driven RKKY decoupling and anomalous 1/R Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction in odd-parity magnets
item.description:
Last authors: Morteza Salehi, Tohid Farajollahpour

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Theoretical study of RKKY and Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction in odd-parity magnets for spintronics.

Tags: #theory #magnetism #spintronics #topological

Abstract: Unconventional odd-parity magnets, characterized by an odd-parity momentum-dependent spin splitting, offer a fundamentally distinct paradigm for non-collinear spintronics. Here, we theoretically investigate the Ruderman-Kittel-Kasuya-Yosida indirect exchange in two-dimensional odd-parity magnets subjected to Rashba spin-orbit coupling. Using an analytical real-space Green's function formalism, we uncover a parity-driven spatial decoupling in the magnetic response. Because of the odd-parity exchange field, the out-of-plane Ising interaction is structurally insulated from the macroscopic magnetic modulation, oscillating isotropically at the shifted Fermi wavevector. Conversely, the in-plane Heisenberg components exhibit pronounced, directionally tunable spatial beating. Beyond collinear exchange, the hybridized bands generate a highly tunable, three-component Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction alongside symmetric off-diagonal anisotropies. We reveal that the out-of-plane chiral twisting is driven by the massive, nonrelativistic momentum shift, while the in-plane chiral components are relativistic. Furthermore, the competition between the nodal geometry and the Rashba gap drives an anomalous, dimension-reducing crossover, in which the in-plane chiral components follow a 1D-like $1/R$ spatial decay along the nodal lines over an extended intermediate-distance window before ultimately recovering the conventional 2D $1/R^2$ asymptote. We demonstrate that these findings hold universally across the odd-parity class by explicitly generalizing our framework to $f$-wave magnets. Finally, numerical tight-binding calculations verify the striking robustness of this parity-driven decoupling against both scalar and random magnetic exchange disorder. These findings establish odd-parity magnets as promising platforms for engineering robust, directionally tunable non-collinear spin textures.

item.description:

Abstract: We introduce graphene nanohelicoids, geometric analogs of graphene nanoribbons, in which the honeycomb lattice is embedded on a helicoidal surface. item.description:
Last authors: Rudolf Bratschitsch, Ermin Malic

Authors: Roberto Rosati, Mohammed Adel Aly, Robert Schmidt, Rudolf Bratschitsch, Ermin Malic

Why: Experimental study of strain engineering of exciton diffusion in WSe2 monolayers.

Tags: #experiment #monolayer #2Dmaterials #excitons #phonons

Abstract: Tungsten-based transition metal dichalcogenides exhibit dark excitons as the energetically lowest states. These are crucial for exciton thermalization and propagation and they dominate low-temperature photoluminescence via the emergence of pronounced phonon sidebands. After a resonant excitation, highly mobile hot dark excitons are formed, which quickly thermalize into an equilibrium distribution. The application of strain modifies the exciton energy landscape and, in particular, the relative energy separation between bright and dark exciton states. The impact of strain on the transient photoluminescence and diffusion of non-equilibrium excitons has remained largely unexplored so far. In this work, we investigate the spatiotemporal exciton dynamics in strained hBN-encapsulated WSe2 monolayers at cryogenic temperatures. We demonstrate that tensile strain abruptly increases the excess energy of hot excitons, thereby accelerating their transient diffusion. We trace this back to suppressed phonon-mediated scattering from bright to dark excitons. Furthermore, we predict a periodic modulation of the transient exciton diffusion in the presence of a compressive strain resulting from strain-driven emission of M phonons. The gained microscopic insights illustrate how strain can be used to engineer transient photoluminescence and exciton diffusion in technologically promising 2D semiconductors.

Abstract: Moir\'e semiconductors provide a physical realization of the Hubbard model. Bandwidth-tuned Mott transitions and complex phase diagrams mimicking those of high-temperature superconductors have been demonstrated near a weak Mott insulating state at half-band-filling. The platform also provides an opportunity to explore the physics of a partially filled Hubbard band at doping densities far away from the Mott insulator, a regime that has remained largely unexplored. Here we report the emergence of an extended strange metal (ESM), in both doping density and twist angle, in a partially filled Hubbard band of twisted bilayer WSe2. These observations distinguish the state from the reported strange metals associated with quantum criticality and favor the viewpoint that it is an intrinsic state of matter. We also report the observation of a new superconducting dome being developed from the ESM but far away from both the Mott insulating state and the van Hove singularity of the material. Our work opens the door to exploring the new regime of partially filled Hubbard bands in the clean limit.

Abstract: Double-layer systems with narrow or flat electronic bands may exhibit spontaneous interlayer coherence, described by a layer-pseudospin ferromagnetic order parameter. item.title: [9] Theory of the intrinsic optical anomalous Hall responses in time-reversal symmetry breaking superconductors
item.description:
Last authors: Jia-Long Zhang, Wen Huang

Abstract: Determining the symmetry of the Cooper pairing in superconductors is a central challenge in condensed matter physics. Time-reversal symmetry breaking (TRSB) is among the most distinctive symmetry-breaking pattern of a superconductor. An important subset of TRSB pairing states, including the topological $p_x+ip_y$ pairing, is expected to exhibit the optical anomalous Hall effect. However, the microscopic ingredients that enable the Hall response and their underlying organizing principle in clean superconductors remain unelucidated. Here, we develop a unified theory for TRSB multiband superconductors possessing inversion symmetry, and establish their intrinsic optical Hall response as fundamentally a quantum-geometric phenomenon. We distinguish unitary and nonunitary TRSB states. Diagrammatically, we identify two classes of processes: single-electron tunneling and Cooper-pair tunneling. Both involve at least one interband tunneling event driven by the interband velocity-which is closely tied to the interband Berry connection. We rigorously prove that interband pairing is a prerequisite for unitary states to generate intrinsic Hall response, whereas it is not absolutely needed for nonunitary states. In nonunitary states with intraband pairing alone, the Hall effect can arise through single-electron tunneling, provided spin-orbit coupling is present. An effective theory obtained by integrating out the hole degrees of freedom reproduces these results and shows how pairing may endow electrons with effective Berry curvature. Finally, through symmetry analysis, we show that intrinsic resonances near the superconducting gap edge are allowed in nonunitary states but forbidden in unitary states. Our work thus establishes quantum geometry as a unifying principle for the intrinsic Hall response in superconductors and provides a guide for distinguishing different candidate TRSB pairings.

item.title: [8] Josephson effect in symmetry-mismatched van der Waals hybrid junctions of NbSe2-Bi2Sr2CaCu2O8+x and NbSe2-Bi2Sr2-xLaxCuO6+y
item.description:
Last authors: Qi-Kun Xue, Ding Zhang

Authors: Yuying Zhu, Ziye Liu, Hongtao Yan, et al.

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Highly relevant vdW junctions involving NbSe2 and cuprate superconductors, addressing pairing symmetry.

Abstract: Coupling superconductors of different symmetries may lead to emergent quantum phenomena but experimental studies on heterojunctions made of lattice-mismatched crystals are scarce. Here, we fabricate Josephson junction by van der Waals stacking NbSe2 flakes on freshly cleaved surfaces of Bi2Sr2CaCu2O8+x or Bi2Sr2-xLaxCuO6+y. We obtain pronounced Josephson currents across the heterojunctions at temperatures below 7 K. The Josephson coupling strength, characterized by the product of the critical Josephson current I_c and the normal state resistance R_n, can reach about 0.3 mV, much exceeding the values previously reported in Pb-Bi2Sr2CaCu2O8+x or Nb-Bi2Sr2CaCu2O8+x junctions. Microwave irradiation induces integer Shapiro steps. We also observe the Fraunhofer diffraction pattern by applying an in-plane magnetic field. We compare our results with the theoretical calculations that take into account the coherent tunneling and the order parameter mixing. Our work demonstrates the hybrid junctions as a distinctive platform for addressing pairing symmetry and emergent quantum phenomena.

item.title: [8] Magnetization and Josephson current coupling drives the Josephson diode effect in FeTe0.55Se0.45 van der Waals junctions
item.description:
Last authors: Gil Young Cho, Gil-Ho Lee

Authors: Seung-Hyun Shin, Cheong-Eung Ahn, Chang-Won Choi, et al.

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Examines nonreciprocal transport in topological superconducting junctions, relevant to magnetic topological physics.

Tags: #experiment #FeTeSe #superconductivity #transport

Abstract: The Josephson diode effect (JDE) reflects symmetry breaking in the current-phase relation (CPR) of Josephson junctions, yet establishing its microscopic origin is often challenging. We investigate the mechanism of the JDE in van der Waals Josephson junctions based on FeTe0.55Se0.45, a platform where superconductivity, topology, and magnetism may coexist at the interface. Our devices exhibit a robust zero-field diode response with asymmetric switching currents. Magnetic-field measurements reveal a hysteretic Fraunhofer pattern and magnetic-resonance-induced voltage feature, evidencing interfacial magnetism coupled to the Josephson current. Microwave response further shows half-integer Shapiro steps with asymmetric evolution, demonstrating contributions from both a second harmonic and a magnetization-induced phase shift in CPR. Numerical simulations combining magnetization dynamics and Josephson phase dynamics reproduce these features, confirming that the JDE originates from interfacial coupling between magnetization and Josephson current. This work provides a transport-based route to pinpoint the microscopic mechanism of the JDE, establishing a platform for exploring magnetically active interfacial superconductivity, and enables the design of nonreciprocal superconducting devices in clean, interface-engineered van der Waals systems.

item.title: [7] Valence-Driven Structural Transformation and Phase Coexistence in Chemically Substituted EuPd2Si2
item.description:
Last authors: Saul H. Lapidus, Theo Siegrist

Authors: Masoud Mardani, Shivani Sharma, Saul H. Lapidus, Theo Siegrist

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Strongly correlated electron physics and phase transitions in Eu-based systems, relevant to broader interests.

Tags: #experiment #EuPd2Si2 #stronglycorrelated

Abstract: EuPd2Si2 serves as an ideal system to probe the interplay between lattice dynamics and electronic instabilities through its tunable valence transition, responsive to temperature, pressure, and magnetic field. Here, we focus on investigating the origin of the temperature-induced europium valence instability in pristine EuPd2Si2, alloyed EuPd2Si1.95Ge0.05, and EuPd2Si1.9Ge0.1 and its correlation with structural responses. Compared with the parent compound EuPd2Si2 which exhibits the europium valence transition at Tv = 143 K, magnetic susceptibility measurements reveal a systematic shift in Tv with Ge substitution, decreasing to 87 K for EuPd2Si1.95Ge0.05. Temperature-dependent synchrotron X-ray diffraction confirms phase coexistence between Eu2+Pd2Si2-xGex and Eu3+Pd2Si2-xGex phases across the valence transition for all samples measured (x = 0, 0.05, 0.10). The pronounced increase in the full width at half maximum (FWHM) well above Tv reflects the gradual nature of the transformation and highlights the role of structural strain in stabilizing the coexisting phases, supporting the presence of a phase-segregated ground state, in contrast to a homogeneous intermediate-valence or mixed-valence state. The variation in Tv across different compositions correlates with changes in lattice parameters, highlighting the robust coupling between the structural and electronic degrees of freedom. The phase diagram suggests an inverse linear relationship between the lattice parameter and Tv, suggesting a possible predictive framework for estimating transition temperatures in other chemically substituted variants of this family.
